semantic_payload.role_interpretation: The user starts with an unresolved, cautious assessment of single-sourcing versus dual-sourcing, balancing the physical risk of a single point of failure against the high defect rates and financial premium of a weaker secondary source. source_evidence.text: I hear “single point of failure” and become uneasy, but then quality shows me the defects created by maintaining two versions and finance shows me what the second source costs.
Paying more for worse present performance is not automatically resilience.
Concentrating a critical board is not automatically reckless.
I need a way to compare the risks we actually have, not the slogans attached to them.

semantic_payload.role_interpretation: The user's final proposed strategy: maintaining a structured 75/25 split with adopted protections, funding a shared interface spec for the replacement design, limiting supplier exclusivity clauses, and deferring the definitive sourcing decision to the 12-month review.

source_evidence.text: We will keep the seventy-five/twenty-five allocation through the twelve-month review, update and test the owned buffer, and count engineering support explicitly.
For the replacement, we will fund a shared interface and validation specification while asking both suppliers to propose implementations; we will not give either an automatic design award.
The first-opportunity clause will have a short deadline and no restriction on parallel work.
At twelve months we will decide using quality, total support cost, redesign progress, and demonstrated recovery—not the original eighteen-percent headline.
